generation.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: transparent 4x4 action sprite atlas, identity/equipment repair only.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET with sixteen original action poses. Image 2 is the canonical paladin master identity and equipment reference. Preserve the target's exact 4x4 grid, sixteen cell positions, character scale, pose silhouettes, two original arms/hands, expressions, action props, clothing, gold cross symbols, face, hair and colors. Do not substitute idle poses and do not redraw an action.

Repair only the missing canonical equipment. The paladin has exactly ONE compact gold warhammer with rectangular red-inset head, at the character's anatomical RIGHT hip (PICTURE LEFT in front view), and exactly ONE small red/gold cross holy book at anatomical LEFT hip (PICTURE RIGHT in front view). Keep the book already present; do not duplicate it or replace action props with it. Match the master hammer shape, size and proportions: short handle, broad compact rectangular head, total length roughly one fifth of character height. It hangs diagonally down/out from the same left waist belt attachment, not as a tall staff or giant mallet. When both original hands are busy, the hammer is belt-holstered and leaves both hands free; do not add a third hand to hold it. In side/prone poses, rotate and foreshorten this same attached hammer with the pelvis, allowing physically correct occlusion by body, hair or props. Keep the head and handle connected. Never move the hammer to the other hip between paired action cells.
All original action props remain distinct from equipped hammer/book: no converting cards, fans, toys, food or paperwork into extra holy equipment. Exactly two anatomical arms and hands, except legal occlusion.
Keep genuine transparent background; no labels, borders, checkerboard, extra decoration, duplicate body parts, or new effects. Preserve every original cell's different action.
This is a 16-angle TURNAROUND, NOT sixteen front poses. Keep every original angle, two open outward palms, head tilt, face, clothing, hair and existing book placement. Never mirror or rearrange the grid. The belt hammer is attached to anatomical RIGHT hip, opposite the existing book. PICTURE LEFT is true only for FRONT views; it changes in rear/profile views.
Cell0 FRONT: full hammer at PICTURE LEFT hip, original book PICTURE RIGHT.
Cells1/2 front-left-quarter: hammer foreshortens on far hip, original near-side book stays visible.
Cells3/4 LEFT PROFILE: hammer mostly hidden on far hip behind torso/hair; only plausible small edge. DO NOT put exposed hammer beside the visible book.
Cell5 REAR-LEFT: a small hammer portion begins emerging at PICTURE RIGHT lower hip through hair.
Cells6/7/8 BACK: one hammer on PICTURE RIGHT lower hip, book on PICTURE LEFT (may partly occlude in hair). No back-left hammer.
Cells9/10 rear-right-quarter: keep hammer on anatomical right/near hip as body rotates, smoothly continuing from rear-right.
Cells11/12 RIGHT PROFILE: hammer on the near hip, foreshortened; book partly hidden on far side. Do not add a second visible book.
Cells13/14 front-right-quarter: hammer turns continuously into the front-view picture-left waist; not teleported to opposite anatomical hip.
Cell15 FRONT: full hammer at PICTURE LEFT hip, original book PICTURE RIGHT, matching cell0.
Same short compact rectangular red-inset gold hammer in all visible angles; handle and head connected, no shrinking to an unrecognizable dot in front view, no giant club. Both original open hands remain empty and no extra hands.
